discovery_leads.title: The Last Ice on Puncak Jaya
discovery_leads.description: Ice near the summit of the Indonesian mountain peak has shrunk to scattered patches too small to flow like glaciers.

discovery_leads.title: A True Halloween Story Treat: The dirt on Oppy’s demise!
discovery_leads.description: On Launch Complex 17-B, Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, the Delta II Heavy launch vehicle jetted toward Mars on 7 July 2003 at 11:18:15 PM, Eastern daylight time. A robotic rover formally named Opportunity , and dearly nick-named “Oppy” was a passenger on the rocket. Oppy’s profession was a robot geologist on assignment for NASA to find water and evidence for past life on Mars.

discovery_leads.title: Branching out: New study reveals when invasive pythons take to the trees
discovery_leads.description: Effective management of invasive species often depends on not only understanding where the species lives, but how it behaves. In Big Cypress National Preserve, USGS scientists are uncovering new insights into the behavior of one of Florida’s most prolific invasive snakes – the Burmese python. A new study provides important context for understanding and managing this formidable snake.

discovery_leads.title: California has lost 60% of its coastal dunes since the 1800s, new study finds
discovery_leads.description: California’s coastal sand dunes are disappearing. A new statewide assessment finds that the state has lost approximately 60% of its coastal dune area since the mid-1800s, as urban development, coastal erosion and changing land uses have dramatically reshaped these important ecosystems.

discovery_leads.title: Media Alert: Low-level Flights to Image Geology over Central Texas
discovery_leads.description: RESTON, Va. – Low-level airplane flights will begin in early November over central Texas to image geology using airborne geophysical technology.

discovery_leads.title: Media Alert: Low-level Flights to Image Geology over Northeastern Iowa and Southeastern Minnesota
discovery_leads.description: RESTON, Va. – Low-level airplane flights will begin as soon as early November over northeastern Iowa and southeastern Minnesota to image geology using airborne geophysical technology.

discovery_leads.title: Media Alert: Low-level Flights to Image Geology over U.S. Virgin Islands
discovery_leads.description: RESTON, Va. – The U.S. Geological Survey will begin low-level airplane flights in November over the U.S. Virgin Islands to image geology using airborne geophysical technology.

discovery_leads.title: Mercury contamination interacts with stress hormones to influence the immune and endocrine systems of adult northern elephant seals
discovery_leads.description: A 10-year USGS collaborative study explores the interactive effects of mercury contamination and stress on northern elephant seals.

discovery_leads.title: Mercury exposure to northern elephant seal pups in utero is high and affected by the oceanic foraging behavior of their moms
discovery_leads.description: USGS researchers led a 10-year collaborative research effort to see how maternal foraging strategies affect the transfer of mercury to their offspring.

discovery_leads.title: Modernizing Landsat Notifications: SNS Topics Replace RSS Feeds
discovery_leads.description: The USGS Earth Resources Observation and Science (EROS) Center uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) topics to notify users when new Landsat Collection 2 data and science products are added to the archive’s cloud-based inventory.

discovery_leads.title: New USGS data release on Kīlauea lava fountain heights
discovery_leads.description: A new Data Release by the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory provides measurements of lava fountain heights during episodes 1–50 of the ongoing episodic eruption in Halema‘uma‘u at the summit of Kīlauea, which began December 23, 2024.

discovery_leads.title: Photo & Video Chronology — Episode 56 of lava fountaining at the summit of Kīlauea
discovery_leads.description: On November 5, 2026, the summit of Kīlauea erupted lava fountains for six hours during the fifty-sixth episode of the eruption that began on December 23, 2024. A lava fountain from the north vent reached up to 660 feet (200 meters) above the ground.

discovery_leads.title: Photo & Video Chronology — Kīlauea summit GPS survey
discovery_leads.description: On November 13, 2026, USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory geologists surveyed the pu‘u that has formed on the summit crater rim from tephra fallout from the ongoing episodic eruption at Kīlauea's summit.

discovery_leads.title: Photo & Video Chronology — Overflight of the summit of Kīlauea
discovery_leads.description: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory scientists conducted a monitoring overflight of Kīlauea summit on November 10, 2026.

discovery_leads.title: Picturing the Unimaginable: Two Artists’ Early Journey into Yellowstone's Untamed Wonders
discovery_leads.description: How can a landscape of vividly colored hot springs and erupting geysers be conveyed when it defies imagination? As part of Ferdinand Hayden’s 1871 survey of Yellowstone, artist Thomas Moran and photographer William Jackson brought Yellowstone’s unimaginable wonder to the world through their paintings and photographs.

discovery_leads.title: Podcast Explores the Links Between Storms and Invasive Species in the Pacific Region
discovery_leads.description: A new podcast episode examines how storms increase the risks posed by invasive species on islands and highlights efforts by the Pacific Islands CASC and the Pacific RISCC Management Network to strengthen regional preparedness and response capacity.

discovery_leads.title: SAWSC Hydrologist Presents at the Biennial Okefenokee Science Symposium
discovery_leads.description: SAWSC Hydrologist Greg Cherry was invited to speak at the Biennial Okefenokee Science Symposium. Cherry presented on the Floridan aquifer system in Coastal Georgia and issues with saltwater intrusion in the Savannah/Hilton Head area and near downtown Brunswick, Georgia.

discovery_leads.title: The spectacular springs of Black Sand Basin
discovery_leads.description: Black Sand Basin, a sub-basin of Upper Geyser Basin, is home to impressive hot springs, frequently active geysers, and fascinating history.

discovery_leads.title: Towards Continental Conservation: A Metapopulation Strategy to Support Collaborative Bison Restoration and Management
discovery_leads.description: Join us for a bison-centric Friday's Findings in honor of National Bison Day (November 7)! Tune in to learn how USGS scientists are helping to inform bison restoration and management.

discovery_leads.title: USGS Awards $1.7 Million to 26 States to Preserve Data for Energy, Groundwater, Minerals Exploration
discovery_leads.description: RESTON, Va . — The U.S. Geological Survey announced $1,685,806 in matching grants to 26 state geological surveys to inventory, catalog and preserve historic geoscientific data and physical samples critical to understanding the nation's energy, groundwater and mineral resources, and mapping geologic hazards like landslides.

discovery_leads.title: USGS Projects World Production Capacity for 8 Critical Minerals from 2026 to 2030
discovery_leads.description: RESTON, Va. — The U.S. Geological Survey released projections of world production capacity for eight critical minerals for the next five years in the second World Minerals Outlook. This is a forward-looking assessment that is part of a larger effort to provide forecasts and scenarios for global mineral supply chains, as directed by the Energy Act of 2020.

discovery_leads.title: USGS Study Outlines Scope and Severity of Bat Fatalities at US Wind Energy Facilities
discovery_leads.description: A new USGS study reveals that an estimated 18.7 million bats have been killed at U.S. onshore wind energy facilities since 1981, far more than previously understood. By analyzing data from hundreds of wind projects, researchers identified the species most vulnerable to turbine collisions and uncovered patterns that could help reduce future bat fatalities.

discovery_leads.title: Volcano Minute — A Quiet Eruption Beneath the Pacific
discovery_leads.description: Beneath the ocean’s surface, submarine volcanoes carry out about 75 percent of Earth’s volcanic activity, but much of what they do remains hidden from view.

discovery_leads.title: Volcano Minute — How tall is that fountain?
discovery_leads.description: When lava fountains have erupted at the summit of Kīlauea, one question always quickly follows: How tall is that fountain?

discovery_leads.title: Volcano Minute — Where does Kīlauea's geochemistry story begin?
discovery_leads.description: Hiking on the boardwalk at Haʻakulamanu, also known as Sulphur Banks, in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, is a multisensory experience.

discovery_leads.title: Volcano Watch — Beneath the boardwalk: the scientific legacy of Haʻakulamanu
discovery_leads.description: Just off the boardwalk at Haʻakulamanu (Sulphur Banks) in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, beneath an unassuming pile of rocks and rubble, lies the beginning of over 100 years of geochemical research at Kīlauea.

discovery_leads.title: Volcano Watch — Ruby seamount: A glimpse into the secret life of a submarine volcano
discovery_leads.description: Submarine volcanoes are enigmatic and mysterious because they are cloaked by the overlying ocean, yet their activity represents 75% of earth’s volcanism.

discovery_leads.title: Volcano Watch — Such great heights: measuring Kīlauea’s lava fountains
discovery_leads.description: “How tall is the fountain?” This is the question that volcano watchers keep coming back to once the lava fountains start at Kīlauea. And there have been plenty of opportunities to ask this, as we’ve now had 56 lava fountains over the past two years at the summit of Kīlauea.

discovery_leads.title: Webinar Series - Fueling Discovery with USGS Wildland Fire Science
discovery_leads.description: Fueling Discovery with USGS Wildland Fire Science is a public webinar series hosted by USGS Wildland Fire Science and the Ecosystems Mission Area. These webinars are meant to provide information on the breadth of USGS fire science used by stakeholders to make decisions before, during, and after wildfires in ecosystems across the U.S.

discovery_leads.title: Where do those mesmerizing beautiful blue colors in Yellowstone’s pools come from?
discovery_leads.description: What’s behind the magnificent clear blue of Sapphire Pool in Biscuit Basin? Or those gorgeous milky blues in the namesake features of Norris Geyser Basin’s Porcelain Terrace?

discovery_leads.title: Wildfires Increased Feather River Water Flow
discovery_leads.description: A new study led by U.S. Geological Survey scientists estimates that the 2020 and 2021 wildfires in northern California increased the amount of water moving through the upper Feather River watershed. With fewer plants using water after the fires, more water stayed in the soil or flowed into streams. The watershed feeds Lake Oroville, which helps supply water to more than 27 million people.

discovery_leads.description: FIFA has joined forces with the United Nations (UN) and the World Health Organization (WHO) in supporting the #BeActive campaign launched on the UN International Day of Sport for Development and Peace to encourage people to be #HealthyAtHome as the world comes together in the fight against COVID-19, today and every day. discovery_leads.description: Rome – More people are going hungry, an annual study by the United Nations has found. Tens of millions have joined the ranks of the chronically undernourished over the past five years, and countries around the world continue to struggle with multiple forms of malnutrition. discovery_leads.title: Billions worldwide living with herpes
discovery_leads.description: About half a billion people worldwide are living with genital herpes, and several billion have an oral herpes infection, new estimates show, highlighting the need to improve awareness and scale up services to prevent and treat herpes. About 13% of the world’s population aged 15 to 49 years were living with herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) infection in 2016, the latest year for which data is available. HSV-2 is almost exclusively sexually transmitted, causing genital herpes. Infection can lead to recurring, often painful, genital sores in up to a third of people infected. discovery_leads.title: Call for action to reduce the harmful use of alcohol
discovery_leads.description: For the first time, delegations from all 193 Member States of World Health Organization (WHO) reached consensus at the World Health Assembly on a resolution to confront the harmful use of alcohol -- which contributes to poor health globally, can devastate families and damage the structure of communities. Facts on alcohol Every year, the harmful use of alcohol kills 2.5 million people, including 320 000 young people between 15 and 29 years of age. It is the eighth leading risk factor for deaths globally, and harmful use of alcohol was responsible for almost 4% of all deaths in the world, according to the estimates for 2004. discovery_leads.title: Children’s story book released to help children and young people cope with COVID-19
discovery_leads.description: A new story book that aims to help children understand and come to terms with COVID-19 has been produced by a collaboration of more than 50 organizations working in the humanitarian sector. With the help of a fantasy creature, Ario, “My Hero is You, How kids can fight COVID-19!” explains how children can protect themselves, their families and friends from coronavirus.

discovery_leads.description: Half of the world’s children, or approximately 1 billion children each year are affected by physical, sexual or psychological violence, suffering injuries, disabilities and death, because countries have failed to follow established strategies to protect them. This is according to a new report published today by the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, UNESCO, the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General on Violence against Children and the End Violence Partnership. “There is never any excuse for violence against children," said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “We have evidence-based tools to prevent it, which we urge all countries to implement.

discovery_leads.title: Countries failing to stop harmful marketing of breast-milk substitutes, warn WHO and UNICEF
discovery_leads.description: A new report by WHO, UNICEF, and the International Baby Food Action Network (IBFAN) reveals that despite efforts to stop the harmful promotion of breast-milk substitutes, countries are still falling short in protecting parents from misleading information.

discovery_leads.title: COVID-19 disrupting mental health services in most countries, WHO survey
discovery_leads.description: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted or halted critical mental health services in 93% of countries worldwide while the demand for mental health is increasing, according to a new WHO survey. The survey of 130 countries provides the first global data showing the devastating impact of COVID-19 on access to mental health services and underscores the urgent need for increased funding. discovery_leads.title: COVID-19 Emergency Committee highlights need for response efforts over long term
discovery_leads.description: The Emergency Committee on COVID-19, convened by the WHO Director-General under the International Health Regulations (2005) (IHR), held its fourth meeting on 31 July. discovery_leads.title: Dead and injured following attacks on Ebola responders in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
discovery_leads.description: Two attacks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo have killed 4 workers responding to the Ebola outbreak and injured 5 others.

discovery_leads.title: Ensuring continuity of TB services during the COVID-19 pandemic
discovery_leads.description: GENEVA As the world comes together to tackle the COVID-19 pandemic, it is important to ensure that essential health services and operations are continued to protect the lives of people with TB and other diseases or health conditions. Health services, including national programmes to combat TB, need to be actively engaged in ensuring an effective and rapid response to COVID-19 while ensuring that TB services are maintained. discovery_leads.title: Global leaders intensify commitment to prevent leading childhood killer - measles
discovery_leads.description: Measles strategy works – Now it must expand to more countries Cape Town Measles Declaration pledges to cut measles deaths by half By 2005, almost half a million children will be saved every year if there are expanded efforts to immunize and protect all children against measles, international health experts declared today. discovery_leads.title: Global polio eradication initiative applauds WHO African region for wild polio-free certification
discovery_leads.description: Today, the Africa Regional Certification Commission certified the WHO African Region as wild polio-free after four years without a case. With this historic milestone, five of the six WHO regions – representing over 90% of the world’s population – are now free of the wild poliovirus, moving the world closer to achieving global polio eradication. discovery_leads.title: Hard fought gains in immunization coverage at risk without critical health services, warns WHO
discovery_leads.description: Shutting down immunization services in the COVID-19 pandemic risks triggering a resurgence of diseases that can be prevented with safe and effective vaccines, warns WHO in the lead-up to World Immunization Week (24-30 April).

The workshop was convened as a result of collaboration between WHO and the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health (ASPPH) and the National Environmental Health Association (NEHA) and was attended by 23 professionals in the United States from health and other disciplines, working in public and environmental health, who wanted to learn more about how to integrate HiAP approaches in both academic and practical settings. Last year, the number of children and adolescents who died was double the total number of adult deaths from AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria combined.
